pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING : POETRY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.5 Guided Writing: Imaginative Writing (2 sessions) • Features of a com
Topic 3.7: Guided Writing : Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing : Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we keep our bodies healthy?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING : POETRY
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing : Poetry helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING : POETRY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing : Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing : Poetry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing : Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing : Poetry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing : Poetry from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing : Poetry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Guided Writing : Poetry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we keep our bodies healthy?
2. How do poems differ from prose texts?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing : Poetry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: compose a poem related to the theme using acquired vocabulary.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
